title: Audio Management Unit and Flight Interphone Amplifier Obsolescence Replacement

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Replacement of the discontinued analogue interphone amplifier and its rack by a supported unit with the same audio interfaces, keeping the existing cabin handsets and the existing wiring untouched.

sections.reason: The supplier of the amplifier gave notice in 2017 that the hybrid audio stage could no longer be sourced and that repair capability would end in 2021. At the time the fleet held four hundred and ten units with a mean time between unscheduled removals of nine thousand hours, which meant an unsupported population for at least fifteen more years of service. A second driver was audio quality: shop investigation of no-fault-found removals found the input stage drifting with temperature, which the crews experience as a hum on long sectors and which no bench test in the manual detects.
sections.description: The amplifier is replaced by a unit with a digital input stage and analogue outputs, mounted in the existing position on a new rack KE27719-48 that carries the same four attachment points. The antenna assembly XADE368523-89 and its inboard equivalent D2350122256689 are retained; the protective sleeve LN112642-3C is renewed at the rack feedthrough because the harness is disturbed. Module 2922RC in the lower position is replaced item for item and transceiver 95RC in the aft position is refitted after a connector clean. The countersunk washer AES832388-10 is used at the rack attachment. Work is in the forward cargo compartment equipment area in zone 133 and in the aft cabin in zone 263. No lining is removed and no wire is cut: the change is confined to the rack, the unit and the two connector shells.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 1.4 kg. Direct current load falls by about eighteen volt-amperes because the new input stage does not carry the analogue bias supply. Fully interchangeable at the aircraft level, since the interfaces are unchanged, but the two units must not be mixed within one aircraft because the sidetone levels differ. The bench test procedure changes and the shop test set is superseded. Cabin crew see no difference at the handset. The illustrated parts figure gains an alternate item with a pre and post modification effectivity.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN S01466. Retrofit takes eight manhours overnight with the forward equipment area open. The removed units are returned and the operator receives credit against the replacement price.
